title: Anchor: one place to carry work forward
notes: Present this as John's working personal system. Anchor is Python-based software on PUTER, reached through browsers over Tailscale. The models run through their provider tools; the local host coordinates work and keeps project artifacts. This presentation explains the current source and recorded behavior, not a fresh full acceptance test. notes: The current product has overlapping views, not a rigid folder tree. The Cave of Wonders is the Aladdin persona's name for the High Seat portfolio home. Active and On deck are attention placements for work items, not separate copies of their project files and not automatic execution commands. Projects is the registry of project homes; an effort may have its own directory and cockpit. Example is fictional to keep the shared deck free of personal project details.

notes: These are capability summaries from local skill cards, not a claim that every task launches all of them. ResearchPrime researches and validates; Gandalf assesses; Jumper/Superjump explore ideas; Crucible plans; Foreman executes a frozen plan with checks and corrections. title: Foundry skills: domain expertise and upkeep
notes: Domain skills vary in implementation: do not imply every entry is the same multi-agent engine. Ramanujan combines mathematical reasoning with checkable certificates/solvers where applicable. Legal Beagle grounds analysis in supplied or retrieved sources; Financial Analyst builds financial models. Literature Review manages source-grounded literature synthesis. Einstein creates accessible study material; Chekhov preserves story continuity and author decisions. Figure Designer produces scientific/technical figures. Tidy-Idy proposes folder organization with reversible handling. Zombie Hunter inspects ownership before acting on orphan processes. Doctor is Anchor's system-health entry point, shown as an adjacent support tool rather than falsely listed as an identical Foundry domain engine. No current clinical/legal/financial advice is being given here.

title: A programmatic skill is a managed workflow
notes: Distinguish a prompt skill from a programmatic agent workflow. ResearchPrime and other engine-backed Foundry tools include code that routes roles, validates structured inputs, checkpoints results, limits iterations and handles failure. Agents supply research, judgment, synthesis or coding inside that workflow. Not all skills have identical machinery. The orchestrator is the coordinating layer, not a promise of fully autonomous unlimited action. Reviewer roles do not automatically establish provider independence. Code determines the stages; the models' reasoning and external tools determine what evidence/findings emerge. The operator may need to correct artifacts and supply the next round input.

title: Research Prime: question → evidence → challenge
notes: This maps the real protocol, not a ResearchPrime run performed for this deck. Step 1 defines the objective, alternatives, falsification criteria and stakes. Step 2 requires the human's frozen-plan decision. Step 3 executes from that plan, with real context isolation only where the host supports and verifies it; otherwise approximated isolation is disclosed. Step 4 grades evidence. The live round driver spawns Skeptic, Contrarian and Analyst review roles. Deterministic tally and stakes governor precede expensive adjudication. Conditional debate handles conflicting independent-origin findings. Judge and Synthesizer then run concurrently when admitted; the judge tests findings against the objective, while synthesis directs improvement. The operator applies fixes and supplies the next round; the diagram does not claim the driver writes all revisions automatically. Completion includes qualified convergence or an honest budget/failure stop, with open issues preserved. engine.mjs is a skeleton and is NOT the canonical live entry point; run-rounds.mjs is.
source: SOURCES: researchPrime/SKILL.md · bin/plan-gate.mjs · run-rounds.mjs · round.mjs · governor.mjs

title: What drives the reviews—and what you configure
notes: Local policy resolves coding_family, review_family and default_cli from Anchor settings, with a mirror for other hosts. The configured providers use subscription CLI transports. Latest/highest supported model policy is separate from task depth. Same-family coding and review is allowed but must be labeled cross_model:false. Do not imply three reviewer personas are three independent model families. In ResearchPrime, findings must trace to the goal, agreement is keyed to claim identity, the tally uses >=2-agree logic, and independence is separately evaluated from origin/family metadata. Medium/high stakes allow the Judge/Synthesizer/conditional debate; low stakes omit those expensive stages. Code distinguishes empty review from a genuine dry round. One-dry-round policy exists in canonical prose, while generic tracker code accepts preregistered thresholds: do not promise a universal fixed number of rounds. Default max-rounds is eight in the documented driver, but budget limits are run controls, not all exposed as GUI sliders.
source: SOURCES: researchPrime governor/round code · Anchor settings · Foundry AGENTS.md
